cards.text: Paul the apostle is wrapping up his letter to the believers in Ephesus (Ephesians 1:1). His last big push starts with one word. Finally. And then he tells them to be strong.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Ephesus to be strong. Strong in whose power?

cards.text: Then Paul tells them to get dressed. Not in an apron, friend. In the full armor of God.

cards.question: Why does Paul want the believers to put on the full armor of God?

answers.text: To stand against the devil's schemes
To win the respect of the city

cards.text: Now, armor usually means a fight with people. Swords, soldiers, somebody up front yelling "CHARGE!"

cards.question: Paul says the believers' struggle is against flesh and blood.
If the believers' struggle isn't against flesh and blood, who is it against?

cards.text: Rulers, authorities, the powers of this world's darkness, and the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. That's a LOT, friend, and the toughest thing I ever go up against is my oven timer, and the timer's WINNING.
So Paul says it again: take up the full armor of God. A day of evil comes, and he wants them ready for it.

cards.question: When the day of evil comes, Paul wants the believers, having done everything, to ___.

cards.text: STAND firm, Paul says, with the belt of truth buckled around the waist. No resting, and friend, I already did my years of resting in a drawer.

cards.question: Paul calls the piece of armor that covers the chest the breastplate of courage.

cards.text: It's the breastplate of righteousness. Then Paul gets down to the feet, and look, I stand on a gold base, so nobody has EVER complimented my footwork.

cards.question: Paul says the believers' feet are fitted with the readiness of the ___ of peace.

cards.text: In addition to all this, Paul says, take up the shield of faith. Every soldier needs one. In my bakery, it's an oven mitt.

cards.question: With the shield of faith, the believers can extinguish all the flaming ___ of the evil one.

cards.text: Flaming arrows! The only flaming thing I ever faced was a batch I forgot in the oven, and friend, I LOST.

cards.question: Paul hands the believers the helmet of salvation, then the sword of the Spirit. What does he say the sword is?

cards.text: The armor's on, but Paul doesn't say go get 'em. He says pray in the Spirit.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers to pray in the Spirit only on the day of evil.
Paul tells the believers to stay alert and keep at it in prayer. Who should they be praying for?

cards.text: Then Paul gets personal. Pray also for me, he says.

cards.question: Whenever Paul opens his mouth, what does he ask the believers to pray he'll be given?

answers.text: Words to boldly make known the gospel
A quick way out of his trouble
Rest from all his long travels

cards.text: Paul calls himself an ambassador for the gospel. Now most ambassadors get a fancy office and a nice car.

cards.question: Paul calls himself an ambassador in ___.
Paul asks the believers to pray that he'll be set free from his chains.

cards.text: Nope, Paul asks for prayer to proclaim the gospel fearlessly, as he should. If that were me in the drawer, I'd have asked for a key, a flashlight AND a ride home.
Then Paul names someone he's sending their way: Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord.

cards.question: Why is Paul sending Tychicus to the believers?

answers.text: To tell them about Paul and encourage them
To collect a gift for Paul's trial
To choose new leaders for their church

cards.text: Then Paul closes the letter with a blessing: peace to the brothers, and love with faith.

cards.question: Where does Paul say the peace and the love with faith come from?

answers.text: God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
Peter and the church in Jerusalem
The prayers of all the saints

cards.question: Paul's final blessing of grace is only for the leaders of the church.

cards.text: Grace to all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with an undying love. That's how Paul signs off, friend, and no, I'm not crying, that's just flour in my eye.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'Paul the apostle is wrapping up…', 'His last big push starts with one word.', 'Finally.' and 'And then he tells them to be strong.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from Ephesians 6:12 or any other verse. It is only Papa Dorin's setup about armor usually meaning a fight with people, yet it cites Ephesians 6:12.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The question says the struggle 'isn't against flesh and blood'. Both wrong answers ('Their unbelieving neighbors' and 'The Roman soldiers') are flesh and blood, so the question itself rules them out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess the name Paul gives the breastplate ('courage' vs 'righteousness'). That is wording the baker hasn't seen and can't reason out, like the 'What does He anoint David's head with?' example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank 'readiness of the ___ of peace' asks the baker to guess the exact wording of the line (gospel, law or kingdom), not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank 'flaming ___ of the evil one' asks the baker to guess the exact word (arrows, torches or spears). A shield blocks spears as well as arrows, so the pick comes down to recalling the wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats 'Flaming arrows!' from the choice card before it and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. It also repeats the joke shape from card 8 (an oven struggle he loses).

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The question's setup, 'Whenever Paul opens his mouth', points straight to 'Words…' and rules out the two wrong answers. The right answer also stands out as the only answer tied to speaking, and its wording ('boldly make known') sounds more like the Bible than the others.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The setup 'most ambassadors get a fancy office and a nice car' signals that Paul's situation is the opposite. That rules out the wrong answer 'glory' on card 7 before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card says Paul is 'sending' Tychicus their way. Paul says he has sent him in Ephesians 6:22, but the card cites only Ephesians 6:21.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card calls Ephesians 6:23 'a blessing'. The text doesn't call it a blessing. Paul just writes 'Peace to the brothers…'. This is the same pattern as the Naomi example.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: The question calls Ephesians 6:24 'Paul's final blessing of grace'. The text doesn't call it a blessing. It reads 'Grace to all who love our Lord Jesus Christ…'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)
